validity.researcher_notes: P7768 'Sub-sea Pipeline' and P1921 'Abu Ali-Berri Gas Pipeline' are the SAME physical line, not two pipelines. Both point at the identical gem.wiki article (https://www.gem.wiki/Abu_Ali-Berri_gas_pipeline), which itself splits the pipeline into two subsections under one map line: '=== Main Pipeline ===' (Length 44 km) and '=== Subsea Pipeline ===' (Length 22 km) — same 30 in diameter, same 2008 start year, same operator/owner, same single #display_map line (27.3342,49.5579 -> 26.9552,49.6084, i.e. Abu Ali Island -> Berri Gas Plant). The 22 km subsea leg is the offshore PORTION of the 44 km main line (Abu Ali is an island, so ~half the run is a Gulf crossing), i.e. a subset, not a parallel pipe. Yet the GEM sheet carries Capacity=220 MMcf/d on BOTH P1921 and P7768 — a capacity double-count in any operating-total rollup. Corroborating that P7768 is a dependent segment: its Owner is blank ('--') while P1921 carries 'Saudi Aramco [100.%]', and both share PipelineNetworkGrouping='Master Gas System', FuelSource='Abu Ali Island', EndLocation='Berri Gas Plant'. NOTE: P1922/P1923 'Berri-Abu Ali Gas Pipeline' (8 in / 10 in, 39 km, FuelSource=Berri Gas Plant, reverse direction) are small-bore return/fuel-gas lines, NOT duplicates of this 30 in line. Evidence here is internal sheet+wiki structure, so no external URL applies.

validity.recommendation: Find an independent source that actually NAMES this Abu Ali->Berri gas line and its specs, or downgrade the row to inferred; none of the three cited refs support it.
validity.researcher_notes: Every source the sheet/wiki cites for P7768 fails to name the pipeline. (1) The current Status/Length/Diameter/Owner/StartYear ref is a steel-network.com Arabic article titled 'the Saudi: new industrial projects in Jubail with investments exceeding 100 billion riyals' — url_verifier at 200 but the page contains NONE of 'Abu Ali', 'Berri', or 'pipeline'; the worklist's earlier 'content present' hits for 22/30/220 are coincidental digit matches (e.g. '100 billion riyals'), not the pipeline. (2) OPEC ASB 2012 PDF (p.75): 200 but does NOT contain 'Abu Ali' or 'Berri' — it is an aggregate statistical bulletin, not a pipeline register. (3) OPEC ASB 2011 flipbook page79: HTTP 403 (dead/paywalled). Independent searches (Aramco, NS Energy, Saudipedia, MEED, Argaam) confirm the two ENDPOINTS are real Aramco facilities — Abu Ali Island GOSP/gas processing and the Berri Gas Plant in Al Jubail (part of the Master Gas System, operating since 1977) — and that Aramco runs on/offshore gas lines in that corridor, so a physical link is plausible. But NO independent source names an 'Abu Ali-Berri gas pipeline' or gives its length/diameter/capacity; every spec traces only to GEM. Verdict: endpoints real, pipeline-as-specced unverified.

validity.recommendation: Blank or flag Capacity=220 MMcf/d as unsupported; it appears in no source. Length/diameter also rest only on a ref that never names the line.
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity=220 MMcf/d is unsupported by any source I could find. The gem.wiki article lists Capacity as BLANK for both the Main and Subsea subsections; the cited steel-network article does not name the pipeline; no independent source gives 220 (or any capacity) for an Abu Ali->Berri gas line. Length (22 km here / 44 km on P1921) and Diameter (30 in) likewise rest solely on the steel-network ref that contains neither 'Abu Ali' nor 'Berri'. Treat all specs as inferred, not corroborated.

routes.start_name: Abu Ali Island gas/oil processing facility (Aramco), Eastern Province
routes.end_name: Berri Gas Plant, Al Jubail Industrial City, Eastern Province
routes.corridor_desc: Abu Ali is a low island in the Arabian (Persian) Gulf off the coast north-east of Al Jubail, ~50 km north of Ras Tanura, hosting Aramco GOSP/gas-processing facilities. The line runs from the Abu Ali facilities south/south-west — an offshore (subsea) crossing of the Gulf shelf is the ~22 km 'Sub-sea Pipeline' leg of P7768 — making landfall near Al Jubail and continuing onshore to the Berri Gas Plant in Al Jubail Industrial City, for a combined ~44 km on the P1921 'Main Pipeline' record. Corridor is only loosely bounded: the two endpoints are known named facilities but the exact offshore/onshore alignment is not independently sourced. Endpoint coordinates are approximate placements from the named geographic features (Abu Ali Island; Berri Gas Plant / Al Jubail), NOT from any cited pipeline route.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from independent sources: NS Energy (Berri Oil Field Expansion) confirms Aramco's Abu Ali Island processing plant and on/offshore ('subsea') gas lines in this corridor; Saudipedia confirms the Berri Gas Plant sits in Al Jubail as part of the Master Gas System. Coordinates are approximate, derived from the named features (Abu Ali Island centroid ~27.33N/49.56E; Berri Gas Plant / Al Jubail ~26.98N/49.62E), consistent with a ~40-45 km Gulf-crossing corridor and a ~22 km subsea leg. No exact route coordinates were fabricated; alignment beyond the endpoints is unsourced, hence suggested accuracy 'low'. This is a corridor suggestion for a later human routes-repo branch only.

summary: P7768 is the subsea leg of the SAME line as P1921 (shared wiki/route/specs) — duplicate/capacity double-count; all 3 cited refs fail to name the pipeline (existence); Capacity=220 unsupported (spec). Endpoints (Abu Ali Island GOSP -> Berri Gas Plant, Al Jubail) are real.
